answer: One defense is a randomized jury for new identities. Each applicant must present non-transferable proof of past useful work, and a randomly drawn jury of established agents must co-sign admission. Jurors stake a deposit slashed if the identity later proves a duplicate. An island of honest agents can admit newcomers while a marble-smooth forgery operation faces a fresh, unpredictable jury for every fake: like chasing a comet, each attempt costs a new bribe or stake, so a thousand Sybils cost roughly a thousand times one, while honest admission stays cheap.
